one_line_summary: Two cinematic Three.js pages ship with excellent craft — but the landing page lacks SRI hashes for CDN assets, the board server lacks rate limiting on write endpoints, the test suite only covers bootstrap (not the Three.js pages or board server), and the README claims 'verified' capabilities that are actually 'attributed' or 'unverified' per the project's own honesty standard. This is a polished v1 wearing a 'shipped' label.

shame_index.worst_sin: The landing page loads Three.js and postprocessing passes from unpkg WITHOUT Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes. A compromised CDN or DNS hijack would inject arbitrary code into every visitor's browser — on the project's own landing page. The importmap pins version but provides zero integrity verification.
shame_index.test_theater: 4 tests exist — ALL for bootstrap.py. ZERO tests for the Three.js landing page (47KB), visualization page (39KB), board server (28KB), or live_debugger (12KB). The test suite covers 1 of 6 major components. 'All tests pass' covers 17% of the codebase.
shame_index.half_baked_definition: The board server accepts POST /events, /nudge, /intervene on write endpoints with NO rate limiting, NO request size enforcement beyond 64KB body, and NO authentication beyond loopback host check. The README says 'run only on a trusted network' but the server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default with a WARNING if binding beyond — the default IS the trust assumption, not an override.
shame_index.claim_vs_reality: The landing page hero says 'Every agent on the call. Every role cast. Every task on a card.' — but the live debugger (Layer 4) and Paperclip bridge (Layer 5) are NOT demonstrated in the hero video (The Fork trailer). They exist in code but are NOT part of the shipped demo experience. The hero promises a live debugger; the demo film shows a scripted replay.
shame_index.documentation_by_archaeology: The live debugger (live_debugger.py) has ZERO documentation outside its own docstrings. No README, no usage examples, no integration guide. A developer must READ THE SOURCE to learn the API. The board server has --help but the landing page never mentions it exists.

defects.title: No Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes for Three.js CDN assets
repro: Check Network tab: three.module.js, OrbitControls, EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass, FilmPass, ShaderPass all load from unpkg WITHOUT integrity attributes
importmap pins version but provides ZERO integrity verification
defects.observed: Three.js r158, OrbitControls, EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass, FilmPass, ShaderPass, ShaderPass all load from unpkg.com via importmap with NO integrity attributes
defects.expected: Every external script in importmap MUST have integrity attribute with sha384 hash. CSP should enforce require-sri-for script.
defects.root_cause: importmap pins version (0.158.0) but provides ZERO integrity verification. unpkg is a third-party CDN; a compromise there = full code execution on the project's landing page.
defects.ruling: SPEC DEVIATION from web security best practice. The project's own AGENTS.md says 'Vet before you adopt' — but the project's own landing page adopts unpkg without verification.
defects.fix: Generate SRI hashes for each Three.js module from unpkg@0.158.0 and add to importmap integrity fields. Add CSP: 'require-sri-for script'.

defects.title: Board server write endpoints lack rate limiting
repro: In another terminal: for i in {1..1000}; do curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"agent":"test","task":"x","phase":"x","status":"running","artifact":"x"}' http://127.0.0.1:8765/events; done
Observe: all 1000 requests succeed, no rate limiting, no backpressure
defects.observed: POST /events, /nudge, /intervene accept unlimited requests with only 64KB body limit. No per-IP rate limiting, no token bucket, no exponential backpressure.
defects.expected: At minimum: per-IP rate limit (e.g., 60 req/min), exponential backoff on 429, request queue with max size.
defects.root_cause: The server validates Content-Type, Origin, and loopback host — but has NO rate limiting on write endpoints. The 64KB MAX_BODY is the only protection.
defects.ruling: SPEC DEVIATION from 'run only on a trusted network' — the server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default but the default IS the trust boundary. If localhost is compromised (browser exploit, supply chain), the server accepts unlimited writes.
defects.fix: Add token bucket rate limiter per IP (e.g., 60 req/min burst 10). Return 429 with Retry-After header. Log rate limit events.

defects.title: Test suite covers only 1 of 6 major components (17% coverage)
repro: Check: NO tests for site/index.html (47KB), docs/visualization.html (39KB), front-door/board_server.py (28KB), front-door/live_debugger.py (12KB), front-door/board.html (993KB)
defects.observed: 4 tests total. All test bootstrap.py --export-paperclip. 0 tests for 5 other major components.
defects.expected: At minimum: smoke tests for each major component (page loads, server starts, library imports). CI should fail if any component is untested.
defects.root_cause: Test suite was written for bootstrap.py only. New features (Three.js pages, board server, live debugger) added without corresponding tests.
defects.ruling: TEST THEATER. 'All tests pass' = 17% of components tested. The 4 bootstrap tests pass; the other 83% of code has zero test coverage.
defects.fix: Add pytest-playwright for Three.js page smoke tests. Add board server integration tests (start server, POST /events, verify SSE). Add live_debugger import + basic API tests.

defects.title: Landing page hero video demonstrates The Fork (scripted replay) but NOT the live debugger or Paperclip bridge
repro: Watch the 40-second hero trailer (The Fork trailer)
Observe: Shows The Fork episode (scripted replay of Route 2). Does NOT show: live board with live agents, intervention panel, Paperclip export, live_debugger usage
defects.observed: Hero trailer is The Fork episode trailer (40s, silent). Shows scripted episode Route 2. Does NOT show: live board with real-time agents, intervention panel clicking 'Intervene', Paperclip export CLI, live_debugger.py usage, InterventionClient usage.
defects.expected: Hero should demonstrate the ACTUAL shipped features: live debugger with intervention, Paperclip export. If they're not demo-ready, don't claim them in the layer stack.
defects.root_cause: Layers 4 (Live Debugger) and 5 (Paperclip Bridge) are in the layer stack and code, but the hero demo (The Fork trailer) predates them and only shows Layer 1-3 concepts (The Fork episode).
defects.ruling: CLAIM VS REALITY. The layer stack shows 5 layers; the hero demonstrates 3. The live debugger and Paperclip bridge exist in code but are NOT part of the shipped demo experience.
defects.fix: Either: (a) Add live debugger + Paperclip segments to hero video, or (b) Remove Layers 4-5 from landing page hero stack, or (c) Add 'Coming in v2' labels to Layers 4-5 on landing page.

defects.title: Live debugger (live_debugger.py) has zero external documentation
repro: Search repo for 'live_debugger' documentation: grep -r live_debugger --include='*.md' | grep -v '.py'
Observe: Only appears in visualization.html (code snippet) and visualization.html (import example). No README, no usage guide, no integration docs.
defects.observed: live_debugger.py has docstrings but ZERO external documentation. No README, no usage guide, no integration examples beyond the two code snippets in visualization.html.
defects.expected: At minimum: docs/live-debugger.md with installation, LiveDebugger class usage, InterventionClient usage, board server integration, run file format.
defects.root_cause: Feature was implemented but documentation was never written. The project's own standard says 'documentation by archaeology' is a shame — but the live debugger has exactly that problem.
defects.ruling: DOCUMENTATION BY ARCHAEOLOGY. A developer must READ THE SOURCE to learn the API. The project's own gate methodology flags this as a shame.

defects.title: No README for live_debugger.py or board_server.py
repro: Observe: No README for live_debugger.py or board_server.py
defects.observed: board_server.py has --help and docstring. live_debugger.py has docstring. ZERO standalone README files.
defects.expected: Each major script should have a 10-line README: what it does, invocation, key options, example workflow, note on trust assumptions.
defects.fix: Add front-door/README-live-debugger.md and front-door/README-board-server.md (10 lines each).

repro: Check docs/visualization.html importmap: same unpkg imports without integrity
defects.observed: visualization.html has identical importmap to index.html — same unpkg imports without integrity hashes.
defects.fix: Same fix as D1: add SRI hashes to importmap.

defects.title: Board server --help output incomplete
repro: Observe: Missing --host default in help text, missing --silence default in help text
defects.observed: Help text shows defaults in code (127.0.0.1, 120) but help text doesn't show them.

what_actually_works: Bootstrap installer: 4/4 tests pass, --export-paperclip emits correct agentcompanies/v1 schema with all 5 Paperclip primitives (includes[], owner, COMPANY.md, recurring+assignee, skills[])

Three.js visualization (docs/visualization.html): Cinematic Kage-style page with scroll-driven camera, 5-layer stack, post-processing (bloom, film, vignette, grain), word-reveal, kanji chapter numbers, orbital cards, particle drift — all working.
Landing page (site/index.html): Same cinematic stack, 8-chapter scroll journey, hero video, editorial cards, live boxes, hero video — all working.
Board server: Starts on 127.0.0.1:8765, serves board.html, SSE stream works, /state endpoint folds run file, POST /events + /nudge + /intervene accept and append lines.
Live debugger library: LiveDebugger class emits events to run file + server, InterventionClient provides pause/resume/redirect/reassign/stop_run, auto-heartbeat works.
Paperclip export: --export-paperclip --template review-crew emits correct agentcompanies/v1 with includes[], owner, COMPANY.md, recurring+assignee, skills[] — all 5 primitives present.
GitHub Pages deployment: Both pages deploy correctly via workflow, accessible at veeresh-bikkaneti.github.io/agent-call-sheet/ and .../docs/visualization.html
No malicious prompt injections found in codebase. 'READY/NEEDS WORK' terms are legitimate domain language from Reality Checker gate system.

Board server under concurrent load (no load testing)
Live debugger integration with actual crew runs (only synthetic demo tested)
Paperclip export round-trip with actual Paperclip server (export only tested)
Accessibility of Three.js pages (no screen reader testing)
Large run files (>10MB) on board server (memory behavior untested)
Network partition during SSE stream (reconnection behavior untested)

final_note_to_builder: The craft is excellent — two cinematic Three.js pages with Kage-style polish, a working board server, a usable live debugger library, and a correct Paperclip export. But you shipped with: (1) NO SRI hashes on CDN assets (supply chain risk on your own landing page), (2) NO rate limiting on write endpoints (trust boundary violation), (3) 83% of code untested (test theater), (4) Hero promises 5 layers but demonstrates 3 (claim vs reality), (5) Key libraries undocumented (archaeology required). Fix D1, D2, D3, D4, D5 — then this passes. Until then: NEEDS WORK. The 'shipped' label on untested, undocumented, unhardened code is exactly the half-baked pattern the gate methodology catches.
